catalog.description: Maximum Mac runner job instances per resolved workflow run, including matrices and nested calls. Telemetry covers 12 event classes, 3 diff classes, same-repository/fork ownership, release architectures and publish switches. inner_measure_reason: one run can occupy several shared Mac slots even when the lifecycle run count stays within its bound. Design bound; analysis reads recorded telemetry only, approximately 2 seconds excluding tests/install; no queue-time claim.

Maximum distinct Mac-spending runs across one ordinary PR push, its base merge, the automation version/changelog PR and merge, release build and downstream smoke fan-out. Explicit manual diagnostics are excluded. Telemetry covers 12 event classes, 3 diff classes, same-repository/fork ownership, release architectures and publish switches. Design bound of 4, approved for plan ci-release-test-cache: the release PR runs all four jobs and its macOS run replays proven results rather than being skipped. The lifecycle spends macOS runs on the ordinary PR, release PR, main cache warmer and release build. The release merge runs no warmer. Analysis reads recorded telemetry only, approximately 2 seconds excluding tests/install; no queue-time claim.

The budget report job from its cold install through the checks, the saved-results read, the history read and the main result upload, the interval ending before the comment post. It protects the turnaround of the required check every pull request waits on.

The longest counted job of each pull request's last-commit CI runs, over the pull requests one release carries, in seconds from GitHub's job timestamps. A pull request reports its own run instead: the longest finished job, the budgets job in progress left out. Holds each check to 30 minutes, because one slow check holds every change behind it; `timeout-minutes: 30` enforces it at PR time.

The most counted jobs any one pull request's last-commit `pull_request` runs started, every workflow, over the pull requests one release carries. A pull request reports its own run instead: that run's jobs, the budgets job in progress counted. Holds this repository's share of the account-wide 20-job concurrency limit that every repository shares.

Room left for one warm run's saves and test results: GitHub's stated Actions-cache allowance, 10 GiB, minus the bytes of every entry, test results (nx-cache-*) included, read over every page of the listing when the command runs, in gigabytes of 10^9 bytes and negative when those bytes are over the line. A family the command names counts only its newest entry, because a working cleanup leaves the previous copy until the next push to main; when a named family holds more than two entries the figure is 0, which reads over, because two is the most a working cleanup leaves. Detail: the allowance, non-result bytes per key family, older copies' bytes, any family over two entries, result entries and bytes, the oldest result's age, the requests the read made and the lowest rate-limit remaining.

Wall-clock seconds one steady-state pass of this repository's declared pool maintenance takes over one ordinary run's worth of superseded cargo builds, as cargo-prune-superseded reports it. Protects how long a regular post-run pass holds one of this repository's warm-pool slots out of service on a host running several dispatches.

The budget report job from its cold install through the checks, the history read, the comment and the main result upload. It protects the turnaround of the required check every pull request waits on.

HTTP requests the Observatory's browser sends per minute with a settled or stopped run open while other runs on the host change, the most expensive of that run's Graph, Overall and node timeline views; detail reports each view's figure, the figure with nothing open under the same activity, and the requests by route. The open run is settled or stopped and its journal does not change; one browser tab. Measured; telemetry analysis only, approximately 2 seconds.

HTTP requests the Observatory's browser sends per minute with a live run open while its journal and other runs' journals grow, the most expensive of its Graph, Overall, node timeline and Channel views; detail reports each view's figure and its requests by route. The open run is live, its journal grown to 116,000 records and appended 50 records per minute, taking the burst; one browser tab. Measured; telemetry analysis only, approximately 2 seconds.

The 95th-percentile time from a record being appended to the open live run's journal until the page has rendered it — the node timeline's row for that record appearing, or Graph, Overall or Channel marking that record's change rendered on its root's data-journal-seq — per record, over every record appended in the window, the slowest of the four views; detail reports each view's p50, p95 and maximum, the p95 during the burst, and frame arrival as a breakdown. Design bound; telemetry analysis only, approximately 2 seconds.

Megabytes the Observatory's browser receives per minute (encoded bytes of every response and event-stream frame), the most expensive page state over nothing open, a settled and a stopped run on Graph, Overall and a node timeline, the live run on Graph, Overall, a node timeline and Channel, and the Host page; detail reports each state's figure, its bytes by route and frame type, and the repeated full-snapshot frames and bytes, at load and after a reconnect. Estimate; telemetry analysis only, approximately 2 seconds.

Maximum server-process-tree CPU seconds divided by the 120 observation seconds and by live tab count, across one-tab and two-tab variants of Graph, Overall, node timeline and Channel on the live run (116,000 records, appending 50 per minute and taking the burst). Includes the server's total CPU, idle work included, with no baseline subtracted; excludes browser and corpus-writer processes. Detail reports total CPU seconds, average total cores, per-tab cores, tab count and page state. Estimate (manager-approved); telemetry analysis only, approximately 2 seconds.

The longest counted job of each pull request's last-commit CI runs, over the pull requests one release carries, in seconds from GitHub's job timestamps. Holds each check to 30 minutes, because one slow check holds every change behind it; `timeout-minutes: 30` enforces it at PR time.

The longest counted job of one release's CD runs (release-plz's run at the release commit and the Release run's six jobs, `publish` up to this check), in seconds. Holds each CD job to 30 minutes, the actionable unit inside the release cycle.

Per pull request one release carries whose merge changes a published path, its last commit's checks (first run created to last job completed) plus its merge to the end of `publish`; the maximum over the release's pull requests, in seconds. Holds a change to 90 minutes from its final checks to its release.

The most counted jobs any one pull request's last-commit `pull_request` runs started, every workflow, over the pull requests one release carries. Holds this repository's share of the account-wide 20-job concurrency limit that every repository shares.
The counted jobs of one release's CD runs, `publish` itself included as the job running this check. Holds the share of the account-wide 20-job concurrency limit this repository's CD takes.

The REST requests the release's own reads cost — the releases listing, the comparison, the closed-pull-request page, the runs at the release commit and the jobs of its CD runs — summed from the onevcs answers' `cost`. Holds the tail's GitHub reads for the release itself, apart from the reads each pull request adds.

The most REST requests any one pull request of the release needed — its runs at head and the jobs of its CI runs — from its `change-checks` answer's `cost`. Holds the reads each pull request adds to the tail, whatever number of pull requests a release carries.

The wall clock of one `just gate` run on a development machine, from the start and end the recipe records on that run. Holds the local gate to the same 30-minute line as each CI check, as a warning, since a machine's timing varies too much to refuse on.

Remote hits as a percentage of attempt-qualified cacheable task/OS/hash executions, excluding local hits. Measure the release PR and same-PR retries and later pushes of the release's counted PRs from existing run artifacts. Report misses, receipt age, promotion failures, unavailable evidence, stored bytes and GitHub requests; absent evidence is not a pass.

catalog.description: Maximum Mac runner job instances per resolved workflow run, including matrices and nested calls. Telemetry covers 12 event classes, 3 diff classes, same-repository/fork ownership, release architectures and publish switches. inner_measure_reason: one run can occupy several shared Mac slots even when the lifecycle run count stays within its bound. Design bound; analysis reads recorded telemetry only, approximately 2 seconds excluding tests/install; no queue-time claim.

Maximum distinct Mac-spending runs across one ordinary PR push, its base merge, the automation version/changelog PR and merge, release build and downstream smoke fan-out. Explicit manual diagnostics are excluded. Telemetry covers 12 event classes, 3 diff classes, same-repository/fork ownership, release architectures and publish switches. Design bound of 4, approved for plan ci-release-test-cache: the release PR runs all four jobs and its macOS run replays proven results rather than being skipped. The lifecycle spends macOS runs on the ordinary PR, release PR, main cache warmer and release build. The release merge runs no warmer. Analysis reads recorded telemetry only, approximately 2 seconds excluding tests/install; no queue-time claim.
The budget report job from its cold install through the checks, the history read, the comment and the main result upload. It protects the turnaround of the required check every pull request waits on.

HTTP requests the Observatory's browser sends per minute with a settled or stopped run open while other runs on the host change, the most expensive of that run's Graph, Overall and node timeline views; detail reports each view's figure, the figure with nothing open under the same activity, and the requests by route. The open run is settled or stopped and its journal does not change; one browser tab. Measured; telemetry analysis only, approximately 2 seconds.

HTTP requests the Observatory's browser sends per minute with a live run open while its journal and other runs' journals grow, the most expensive of its Graph, Overall, node timeline and Channel views; detail reports each view's figure and its requests by route. The open run is live, its journal grown to 116,000 records and appended 50 records per minute, taking the burst; one browser tab. Measured; telemetry analysis only, approximately 2 seconds.

The 95th-percentile time from a record being appended to the open live run's journal until the page has rendered it — the node timeline's row for that record appearing, or Graph, Overall or Channel marking that record's change rendered on its root's data-journal-seq — per record, over every record appended in the window, the slowest of the four views; detail reports each view's p50, p95 and maximum, the p95 during the burst, and frame arrival as a breakdown. Design bound; telemetry analysis only, approximately 2 seconds.

Megabytes the Observatory's browser receives per minute (encoded bytes of every response and event-stream frame), the most expensive page state over nothing open, a settled and a stopped run on Graph, Overall and a node timeline, the live run on Graph, Overall, a node timeline and Channel, and the Host page; detail reports each state's figure, its bytes by route and frame type, and the repeated full-snapshot frames and bytes, at load and after a reconnect. Estimate; telemetry analysis only, approximately 2 seconds.

Maximum server-process-tree CPU seconds divided by the 120 observation seconds and by live tab count, across one-tab and two-tab variants of Graph, Overall, node timeline and Channel on the live run (116,000 records, appending 50 per minute and taking the burst). Includes the server's total CPU, idle work included, with no baseline subtracted; excludes browser and corpus-writer processes. Detail reports total CPU seconds, average total cores, per-tab cores, tab count and page state. Estimate (manager-approved); telemetry analysis only, approximately 2 seconds.

The longest counted job of each pull request's last-commit CI runs, over the pull requests one release carries, in seconds from GitHub's job timestamps. Holds each check to 30 minutes, because one slow check holds every change behind it; `timeout-minutes: 30` enforces it at PR time.

The longest counted job of one release's CD runs (release-plz's run at the release commit and the Release run's six jobs, `publish` up to this check), in seconds. Holds each CD job to 30 minutes, the actionable unit inside the release cycle.

Per pull request one release carries whose merge changes a published path, its last commit's checks (first run created to last job completed) plus its merge to the end of `publish`; the maximum over the release's pull requests, in seconds. Holds a change to 90 minutes from its final checks to its release.

The most counted jobs any one pull request's last-commit `pull_request` runs started, every workflow, over the pull requests one release carries. Holds this repository's share of the account-wide 20-job concurrency limit that every repository shares.
The counted jobs of one release's CD runs, `publish` itself included as the job running this check. Holds the share of the account-wide 20-job concurrency limit this repository's CD takes.

The REST requests the release's own reads cost — the releases listing, the comparison, the closed-pull-request page, the runs at the release commit and the jobs of its CD runs — summed from the onevcs answers' `cost`. Holds the tail's GitHub reads for the release itself, apart from the reads each pull request adds.

The most REST requests any one pull request of the release needed — its runs at head and the jobs of its CI runs — from its `change-checks` answer's `cost`. Holds the reads each pull request adds to the tail, whatever number of pull requests a release carries.

The wall clock of one `just gate` run on a development machine, from the start and end the recipe records on that run. Holds the local gate to the same 30-minute line as each CI check, as a warning, since a machine's timing varies too much to refuse on.

Remote hits as a percentage of attempt-qualified cacheable task/OS/hash executions, excluding local hits, with base_moved tasks counted as misses. Detail: misses by class (throttled, failed, evicted, never_promoted, base_moved), attempts whose evidence is unavailable, receipt ages and requests.

Room left for one warm run's saves and test results: GitHub's stated Actions-cache allowance, 10 GiB, minus the bytes of every entry, test results (nx-cache-*) included, read over every page of the listing when the command runs, in gigabytes of 10^9 bytes and negative when those bytes are over the line. A family the command names counts only its newest entry, because a working cleanup leaves the previous copy until the next push to main; when a named family holds more than two entries the figure is 0, which reads over, because two is the most a working cleanup leaves. Detail: the allowance, non-result bytes per key family, older copies' bytes, any family over two entries, result entries and bytes, the oldest result's age, the requests the read made and the lowest rate-limit remaining.

Wall-clock seconds one steady-state pass of this repository's declared pool maintenance takes over one ordinary run's worth of superseded cargo builds, as cargo-prune-superseded reports it. Protects how long a regular post-run pass holds one of this repository's warm-pool slots out of service on a host running several dispatches.
